How to Refer Us — 1st Buyer Interaction
The exact script an agent should use the moment they get a buyer — via text, email, or verbally, same script either way.
Send to Client:
"[Buyer Name], to ensure that you're 100% safe, secure, and set up for success moving forward with the home search, I'm going to have the Daniel Sa Team at NFM Lending reach out to you directly to get the process started. Everybody on the team does a WONDERFUL job and will provide you with important information that guarantees you're prepared to move quickly with the right home becomes available. They will educate you on every financing option available so you can make an informed decision on what aligns best with your goals. You can expect to hear from them within the next few hours. Please let me know if you have any questions in the meantime. Thank you so much!"
Send an email to the Daniel Sa Team (sateam@nfmlending.com) with the borrower's information:

Contract & Closing CallsListing agent, buyer agent, and clear-to-close 3 scripts + guide
Listing Agent Conversion Guide
Turn every eligible transaction into a retained Realtor meeting opportunity
This is demonstrative selling, not a cold pitch. You already have a transaction, a reason to call, and multiple chances to show the listing agent how the team operates.
Scoreboard: retained Realtor meetings per closed purchase transaction. A training example showed 74 retained meetings from 357 purchase closings — the opportunity was not more transactions, it was executing the conversion moments already available.
Why listing-agent conversions get missed ▾
• Never ask, or ask after the transaction when urgency is gone.
• Execute well but never intentionally connect performance to a meeting.
• Use generic follow-up instead of a defined script and cadence.
• Earn the meeting with a commitment close, then fail to call and collect it at CTC.
Best posture: neither pushy nor passive. Ask early, deliver what matters, and collect the meeting before funding.
CHECK
Run the active-agent search first. If they already work with an NFM LO, protect that relationship.
ASK EARLY
Use the intro call to learn what matters and secure the conditional 15-minute meeting.
DELIVER
Call personally at appraisal-at-value and CTC. Do not let automation own the good-news moments.
COLLECT
At CTC, remind them the promise was delivered and schedule the retained meeting.
Do not overlook the transaction coordinator: capture them and any other team contact in Encompass. Their experience influences the whole office.
Under Contract Call (Listing Agent)
Call the listing agent as soon as a deal you're the buyer's lender on goes under contract. Set the tone early — this is your first real touchpoint with them on this file.
"Hey [Agent Name], this is [Your Name] from the Daniel Sa Team at NFM Lending. I'm calling about your listing at [Property Address], which has just gone into contract. I'm the lender representing the buyer. First, I have a couple of questions about the transaction, I want to make sure we have a smooth process. Does that sound good? Congratulations again on the sale."
Discovery questions to cover:
  • Will this be remote, mail-away, POA, or otherwise non-standard?
  • What is your preferred communication method: call, text, or email?
  • Which milestones do you specifically want updates on?
  • Is there anything you are concerned about or want us watching closely?
  • Is this a simultaneous closing or does the seller need these proceeds for another purchase?
  • Who else on your team, including a transaction coordinator, should we keep informed?
"Our team is available nights and weekends, so I'm going to send you a quick text with my contact info. Please don't hesitate to reach out anytime if you or your seller need anything."
Commitment close — ask on the intro call:
"If we can deliver a smooth transaction and have the loan clear to close at least three days before closing, can I earn 15 minutes of your time to talk about how we might grow our businesses together?"
After the call: save the TC/other contacts in Encompass, send a separate digital business card/contact card, and document communication preferences and concerns. The appraisal-at-value and CTC are your two best direct-call moments.
Under Contract Call (Buyer's Agent)
Call the buyer's agent once the file goes under contract. This call sets the tone for how you will work together throughout.
"Hey [Agent Name], this is [Your Name] from the Daniel Sa Team at NFM Lending. I'm calling about [Buyer Name]'s contract on [Property Address] — congratulations to you and your buyers for going into contract! I wanted to reach out personally and introduce myself. I'll be your main point of contact throughout the transaction and our team is here to support you every step of the way."
Questions to cover:
  • Are there any concerns or anything we should know going in?
  • What's the best way to keep you updated throughout the process — text, email, calls?
  • Regarding the closing date — we want to make sure we stick with the contracted date. We do not move up closing dates. Once we are clear to close, if all parties are in agreement we can revisit at that point.
"Our team is available nights and weekends, so I'm going to send you a quick text with my contact info. Please reach out anytime. We are going to take good care of your buyer."
If they don't already work with us regularly, close for a meeting before ending the call: "I'd love to sit down sometime, even just 15 minutes, to see if it makes sense to work together."
After the call, send a follow-up text with your contact info.
CTC Call
Process: call the agent, leave a voicemail if no answer, follow up with a text if still no response.
"Hi [Agent Name], this is [Your Name] with the Daniel Sa Team at NFM Lending. Congrats on getting [Buyer/Property] to clear to close! I wanted to check in personally, was there anything that went really smoothly for you, or anything we could've done better on our end?"
For an eligible listing agent, use CTC to collect the meeting you earned. If they agreed to the commitment close earlier, remind them the team delivered and put the 15 minutes on the calendar. If they do not answer, leave a voicemail asking for a callback rather than only sending an FYI.
"We delivered what we promised and we're clear to close. I'd love to collect those 15 minutes we talked about — does [day/time] or [day/time] work better?"
Prospecting & Cold OutreachCold call opener, objections, and no-answer follow-up 3 scripts
Cold Call — Opening Script
Before you dial: Pull up RETR and look them up. Find a recent sale or listing and mention it in your opener — "I saw your listing at [address] just closed, congrats!" It makes the call personal and shows you did your homework.
Goal: introduce yourself, explain how we support agents, and schedule a 20-minute meeting.
"Hey [Agent Name], I wanted to reach out and introduce myself. We love working alongside agents to help buyers better understand their financing options, create listing-specific payment strategies, and explore creative financing options to help ensure you and your clients are winning in this market. I would love to learn more about your business and explore ways we can support you. Would you be open to a quick 20-minute meeting sometime next week?"
When scheduling — offer two options:
"Would Tuesday at 11:00 or Thursday at 2:00 work better for you?"
Cold Call — Common Responses
What's the meeting about?"We'd love to learn more about the clients and areas you serve, what you're currently focused on growing, and where additional lending support may be helpful. We can also share some of the financing strategies and listing resources we provide to our agent partners."
Already have a lender"That's completely understandable, and we're not asking you to replace a relationship that's working well. We'd simply love the opportunity to introduce ourselves and become an additional resource when you need a second opinion, have a challenging scenario, or need extra support. Would you still be open to a 20-minute meeting?"
Send me some info"Absolutely. I want to make sure I send something relevant. Would buyer financing options, listing-specific payment strategies, or solutions for more challenging scenarios be most helpful? I'll send that over today. Would it be okay if I follow up with you on [day]?"
I'm busy right now"No problem at all, I completely understand. Would there be a better time for me to call you back, or would it be easier if I sent you a quick text?"
Not interested"I completely understand. Thank you for taking my call. I'll send you my contact information in case you ever need an additional lending resource or a second opinion on a scenario."
No Answer — Follow-Up Text
Send immediately after the missed call.
"Hey [Name], this is [Your Name] with the Daniel Sa Team at NFM Lending. I just tried to give you a quick call to introduce myself. We love working alongside agents to support their buyers, create listing-specific payment strategies, and explore creative financing options to help you and your clients win in this market. I would love to connect for a quick 20-minute conversation. Do you have any availability next week?"
New Agent Follow-Up4-week gifting cadence, commitment ask, and accountability follow-up 2 guides
Gifting Campaign Scripts (4-Week Cadence)
Always try a call first. If no answer, follow up with a text.
Week 1: Break the Ice
Call:
"Hey [Agent Name], this is [Your Name] with the Daniel Sa Team at NFM Lending. I wanted to follow up after our meeting. It was great connecting with you and I'm excited to work together. How has your week been going?"
Text if no answer:
"Hey [Agent Name], this is [Your Name] with the Daniel Sa Team at NFM. Great meeting with you. Looking forward to working together. Here to support you and your buyers."
Week 2: Value Touch
Call:
"Hey [Agent Name], it's [Your Name] with the Daniel Sa Team at NFM. I've been thinking about your business and wanted to share something I think will be useful for you. [share resource or market update]. Would you have a few minutes this week to connect?"
Text if no answer:
"Hey [Agent Name], it's [Your Name] with NFM. I have something I think will be useful for you. [resource]. Let's connect this week!"
Week 3: Opportunity Call
Call:
"Hey [Agent Name], it's [Your Name] with the Daniel Sa Team at NFM. I've really enjoyed getting to know you. Do you have any buyers right now we can help with? We would love to earn your business."
Text if no answer:
"Hey [Agent Name], it's [Your Name] with NFM. Do you have any buyers we can help with right now? We would love to earn your business."
Week 4: Accountability Follow-Up
Call:
"Hey [Agent Name], it's [Your Name] with the Daniel Sa Team at NFM. Wanted to connect and see how your business is going. Do you have any buyers or listings we can support? We are committed to being your go-to team and we are here whenever you need us."
Text if no answer:
"Hey [Agent Name], it's [Your Name] with NFM. Do you have any buyers or listings we can support right now? We are here whenever you need us."
Note: Replace [resource or market update] in Week 2 with something specific to that agent. The more relevant it is to their market or situation, the better it lands.
New Agent Meeting — Commitment & 4-Week Follow-Up
The most common failure mode: great meeting, agent signs up for the mailing list, nothing else happens. This framework closes that gap. The commitment ask is the single most important moment — get it every time, no exceptions.
The Commitment Ask — end of every new agent meeting
"Do I have your commitment to send me the next two to three leads that come your way?"
Deliver this while looking them in the eye and shaking their hand. This creates a spoken agreement that is genuinely difficult to break without consciously going back on their word. Ending with a vague "let me know if I can ever help" puts zero pressure on the agent and gives you no leverage to follow up on. Getting a lead within the first 30 days is critical — after that window closes, the agent has usually reverted to their previous lender and reconverting them becomes exponentially harder.
The 4-Week Follow-Up Structure
Week 0 — Day of the meeting
Send the How to Refer template. Add them on social media. No ask yet — pure value delivery.
Week 1 — Break the walls down
Send a relatable meme or short video — nothing salesy. Just staying on their radar in a human way.
No direct ask. Goal is to make them smile and remember you.
Week 2 — Value touch, still no ask
Send something relevant — market update, sales meeting content, or a financing strategy tip. Nothing that asks for a lead.
Patience here pays off in week 3. Two touches, no pressure — this is what separates you from the LO who emailed three times in a row asking for business.
Week 3 — First lead ask, paired with a unique product
"Hey [Agent], I was thinking about you — do you have any buyers who've been told no elsewhere? We have a 1099 program / bank statement option / portfolio loan that might be worth a look. Also, did anyone come to mind since we met that I could help with?"
Lead with the unfamiliar product, not a well-known one. Every agent has heard of bank statement and DSCR — leading with something more unique (1099, portfolio program) signals you have tools others don't and gives them a specific reason to think of a client.
Week 4 — Accountability call
"Hey [Agent], I wanted to circle back — when we met, you committed to sending me the next couple of leads that came your way. Is there anyone you're working with right now I could help with?"
If they push back or go quiet:
"Did I do something wrong?"
This surfaces the real reason almost every time — fix it, or pivot: "Would you be open to just introducing me to whoever you're currently working with? I'd love the chance to earn a second opinion."
Existing Partner GrowthRetention, feedback, and pipeline review 1 script + guide
For Existing Partners — shifting to earning 100% of their business
"What's one thing we could do better to make working together easier for you?"
Invites specific, actionable feedback and deepens trust simultaneously. The agent who answers this honestly is the one you'll earn 100% of business from.
Pre-Approval Pipeline Guide
Protect the buyers already earned before defaulting to “more leads.” Generic check-ins create a silent pipeline leak; every touch should create an opportunity around a property, payment, showing, or changed timeline.
Why the pipeline review matters: in one training test, sending Realtors their recent pre-approved-buyer lists generated 12 referred leads and 10 new applications over a weekend. Treat the existing pipeline as a growth channel, not just a service task.
Week 1
Call about questions on strategy/programs and identify anything that changed.
Weeks 2–3
Text around showings/properties; offer a concrete payment scenario.
Week 4
Take a deliberate break to prevent contact fatigue.
Weeks 5–8
Repeat purposeful touches, then move to 60-day re-engagement.
When the buyer says nothing fits the price point:
"Is there a property that caught your eye but might be a little more than what you wanted to spend?"
Realtor pipeline review — ask five questions per buyer:
  1. Are they actively looking?
  2. Do they have showings this week?
  3. Have they gone stalled?
  4. What is preventing movement?
  5. What is the next action and who owns it?
Buyer switched agents? Send the new agent the updated pre-approval with highlights, call immediately to introduce yourself and offer help, then create a three-way text with the buyer and new agent. Treat it as a warm new-agent conversion opportunity.
Encompass: the Pre-Approved Buyer box needs to be checked so the pipeline can be pulled by Realtor and the correct Total Expert journey can run.
Initial Realtor Meeting FrameworkControl the meeting, understand the agent, prove value, and earn the next 2–3 buyers training
Goal: establish control, learn what matters to the Realtor, and demonstrate value so the team becomes the obvious lending choice. The activation target is a first lead within 90 days.
1 · OPEN WITH CONTROL
Use a strong 30-second intro, a quick honor statement, and a clear outline for the conversation.
2 · LEARN FIRST
Do not jump to rates or products. Learn their priorities, pain points, current lender setup, and business goals.
3 · PROVE VALUE
Connect our service to what they said matters: speed, communication, access, execution, and business-growth support.
4 · CLOSE FOR ACTION
Ask for the next 2–3 buyers and leave with a defined follow-up plan, not a vague “keep in touch.”
Needs analysis
Use FORGE-style rapport questions around family, occupation, recreation and goals, then transition into their business. Listen, take notes, and tailor the rest of the meeting to what they tell you.
Proof + collateral
Use the Standards of Service plus approved collateral such as 10 Ways to Win, 5-Year Rate Drop Watch, and Multiple Offer Win. Reinforce immediate lead response, strong access, proactive communication, and the team’s fast-close capability.
Affiliated-lender objection
Research the agent before the meeting. If they use an affiliated lender, position the team as specialized expertise and a strong second option rather than attacking the existing relationship. Use proof and case studies, not pressure.
“I’d love the opportunity to earn the next two or three buyers that come your way so you can experience how we communicate and execute. Can I earn that chance?”
First-lead conversion: once the first referred buyer has a great experience, ask the buyer to text the Realtor with positive feedback. That third-party proof strengthens the relationship faster than another sales pitch.
How to Compete: Buyer StrategyOffer strength, appraisal strategy, fast closings, contingencies, and seller-friendly terms training
Core idea: help the buyer and Realtor build a stronger offer without defaulting to price alone. The lending partner should be active in the offer process with scenarios, guidance, and direct follow-up when appropriate.
Top offer levers: appraisal gap / appraisal waiver · over asking / escalation clause · fast closing / reputable local lender · non-contingent pre-approval when eligible · extended possession / rent-back.
APPRAISAL GAP / WAIVER
An appraisal gap is a buyer commitment to cover a short appraisal by a defined amount. An appraisal waiver is property-specific and eligibility must be verified before the offer is submitted.
ESCALATION / OVER ASKING
Prepare clients for the payment impact before they write aggressively. Scenario work helps the Realtor have the difficult conversation before offer time.
FAST CLOSING
Speed is a team effort: get the fully executed contract immediately, disclosures signed quickly, and the appraisal ordered promptly so the file can move without avoidable delay.
CONTINGENCY SOLUTIONS
Explore recasting, bridge financing, eligible retirement assets, gifts, or primary-residence rental conversion when a home-sale contingency is creating friction.
Appraisal strategy
An appraisal gap creates a minimum seller guarantee if value comes in short. A waiver can make the offer cleaner when the property and borrower qualify. Always run the specific property and current guidelines before presenting a waiver as available.
Fast-close execution
The lender's reputation matters in a multiple-offer environment. Set expectations at contract acceptance: executed contract the day it is ratified, disclosures within 24 hours when possible, and appraisal ordering within 24 hours when required.
Recast vs. bridge financing
Recast: can preserve flexibility and lower the payment after additional principal is applied, but the buyer must have another way to fund the purchase initially. Bridge: can unlock equity from the current home for the next purchase, but adds cost and temporary financing. Match the strategy to the client's assets, timing, and qualification.
Seller-friendly structure
Extended possession or a rent-back can solve a seller timing problem and make an offer more attractive without only increasing price. Confirm current occupancy and program limits before advising on the structure.
Future refinance value
When a current refinance-credit or rate-drop program is available, use it to help clients understand that today's rate does not have to be the forever rate. Verify current eligibility, dates, credits, and program terms before quoting.
Use current guidelines. Product eligibility, waiver rules, fast-close programs, refinance incentives, occupancy limits, and pricing can change. Use this as strategy training and verify current terms before quoting them to a client or Realtor.

Clear ownership lanes

  • RM: partner portfolio health, relationship rhythm, retention and growth.
  • LP2: client + transaction experience and buyer/buyer-agent execution.
  • LP1: conversion/front-end support and early buyer movement.
  • Production leadership: visibility, coaching and accountability.

Weekly operating rhythm

  • Monday: set up the week and review production plan.
  • Tuesday–Thursday: execute, communicate and move files/buyers.
  • Friday: inspect WIP, unresolved gaps and next actions.
  • Use early-warning status: Green = current, Yellow = correctable miss, Red = repeated/material miss.

Execution standards

  • Required leads entered into CRM.
  • Required under-contract buyer-agent/client updates completed from each LP’s own worklist.
  • Mandatory conversion steps executed and documented.
  • File Integrity starts at Ready for Pack Out; respond quickly to daily Processing/LOA asks.
Operating rule: a zero-tolerance designation creates an accountability event; it is not averaged away by production elsewhere. The tracker should show the missed standard, owner, corrective action and next result.

Target: 1 opportunity per $250 spent each month — either a buddy intro or warm lead. Goal: 80%
Lead Definition
  1. Agent speaks to buyer
  2. Buyer is expecting our call
  3. Agent sends an email (preferably) or text with buyer's contact (name, phone, email)
Realtor Introduction Definition
Realtor sends group text with another agent and the LO with the following script: "Meet (LO), he is my preferred lender and he is awesome. I figured you two should meet at some point. I'll let you take it from here..."
